name: Fiesta colourware
summary: Solid-colour dinnerware for the American home. A round Art Deco shape with concentric rings is glazed in one strong colour, and the buyer mixes the colours of the open stock. The first red glaze held uranium.

philosophy.core_thesis: One simple, ringed shape in a set of strong glaze colours lets every buyer build a table of their own, one piece at a time.
design_principles: Use one shape family with concentric rings in relief on the rim and the foot.
Glaze each piece in one solid colour, and offer 5 or more colours in the first year.
Sell the line as open stock: each piece is sold by itself, and the buyer picks the colour.
Make the glaze thick and semi-opaque so that the colour covers the body.
Fire a red glaze with uranium oxide to get an orange-red.
Leave the base unglazed in a ring where the piece stood in the kiln.
Add a new colour from time to time to keep the line new.
anti_patterns: A printed or painted pattern on the face
A white porcelain body with a thin glaze
A gilt rim and a floral band
A pastel matt colour with a soft, uneven tone

form.shape: Round plates, bowls, covered casseroles, pitchers, tumblers and shakers, all with the same concentric rings.
form.profile: A round, simple form; the plate has a flat well and a low wall, and a bowl has a rounded body.
form.foot_and_rim: A narrow foot ring, unglazed at the base; the rim is round, with 2 to 3 raised rings.
form.proportion: Plate diameter 15 to 28 cm and wall 5 to 7 mm thick; the rings are about 1 mm high and 6 mm apart.
rules: Put the rings on the rim of every plate and bowl in the line.
Keep the form round and simple, with no pattern on the face.
Glaze the whole visible surface in one colour.

bodies.rule: Use a semi-vitreous white earthenware that takes a thick, bright glaze. Do not use porcelain: the line has to be cheap and strong.

methods: slip casting of pitchers and shakers
forming.joins: Handles are cast or pressed and luted with slip; a lid sits on a plain rebated seat.
forming.details: Three small marks of the kiln stilts on the base, a ring of bare body at the foot, and a mould seam on cast parts.

glaze.pattern: No pattern: solid glaze colour on a shape with concentric rings in relief.
glaze.gloss: Bright gloss, about 85 to 95 GU, with a semi-opaque colour.
glaze.wear: The glaze crazes in a fine net, and the cutlery marks the well in grey; the colour stays strong.

palette.strategy: A set of strong solid colours, each in its own tone: red, cobalt blue, green, yellow and ivory, then turquoise.

firing.kiln: A tunnel kiln with saggars; a biscuit firing at high heat and a glost firing at a lower heat.
processes: dipping or spraying in coloured glaze
firing.scale: A large factory that made tens of thousands of pieces a day, in a single open-stock line.
firing.signs: Stilt marks on the base, a ring of bare body at the foot, and an even colour from piece to piece.

pieces.form: Plate with concentric rings on the rim, in a solid red glaze
Oval platter with a ringed rim, in cobalt blue
Round shaker pair with a ring at the shoulder, in yellow
Footed salad bowl with rings at the rim, in turquoise

positive: concentric rings in relief on the rim
semi-opaque red, cobalt, yellow and turquoise glaze

canonical_works.maker: Frederick Hurten Rhead, Homer Laughlin China Company

canonical_works.work: Fiesta red glaze with uranium oxide

emotion.target_response: A bright, easy cheer: the viewer sees strong colours on a plain shape and wants to mix a table of their own.

use_cases: a retro American kitchen or diner scene
avoid_when: the brief wants a quiet neutral set
the brief wants a painted or printed pattern
the brief needs food-safe modern glaze for use

modifiers.how: Change the glaze to a matt or satin pastel and replace the rings with a soft, flowing curve.
Add hand-painted bands and motifs over a white ground, and keep the round form.
Change the colour glaze to white, change the body to porcelain, and drop the rings.

wall_thickness.note: A semi-vitreous earthenware wall is thicker than porcelain.
